claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in nanoscale FCC/BCC HEA multilayers is primarily governed by stress-induced, interface-mediated phase transformations.
Repeated interactions between dislocation slip and nanolayer interfaces trigger a gradual phase transformation.
Compositional complexity, lattice distortion, and short-range order at FCC/BCC interfaces create locally variable energy barriers.
The proposed transformation can produce HCP-like regions or deformation twins.
The transformed or twinned interface regions are softer than the starting interface regions.
The starting coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC HEA layers with well-defined interfaces.
The starting FCC/BCC interfaces possess significant lattice distortion and inherent short-range order.
Interfaces act as sites for dislocation accumulation.
Local modifications of short-range order at interfaces lower the energy barrier for stress-induced phase transformation.
Under sustained load, dislocations nucleate and propagate through the HEA layers.
Dislocation interactions with chemically complex, distorted interfaces cause local destabilization and stress concentration.
Stress concentration together with short-range-order heterogeneity triggers phase transformation or twinning at or near FCC/BCC interfaces.
The newly formed phase accommodates additional plastic deformation and produces a progressive, self-sustaining flow mechanism.
Sustained loading will produce gradually increasing plastic strain accompanied by interfacial HCP-like regions, twins, or altered dislocation structures.
The creep rate may exhibit a transition when transformation-controlled plasticity begins.
The mechanism applies only while the layers remain nanoscale, coating integrity is retained, and gross instabilities such as layer coarsening do not occur.
Pre-annealing can modify the interfaces by relaxing short-range-order effects.
Absence of transformation signatures, or unchanged creep behavior after interface chemistry is varied, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
